observations: Photo 0: close-up of a diesel engine valve cover reading 'DAF 24 VALVE' in cast lettering, with a separate stamped plate reading 'DAF' and a number '1428063'.
Photo 0: engine bay area shows oxidized, oily metal, worn fan blade, belts, and hoses with surface corrosion.
Photo 1: the same type of inline engine sits outdoors on bare ground, partly covered by a dirty tarp, surrounded by other pulled engines, transmissions, and axle parts.
Photo 2: wide shot shows multiple DAF-marked inline engines stacked/stored together in an open yard, tarps overhead, no building or test rig visible.
No oil pan, wiring harness, turbo, or ECU fully visible in any photo; no fluids, no running state, no gauges or test leads shown.
No photo shows the engine mounted in a chassis or attached to a gearbox/bellhousing as part of a complete 'trailer head'.

identity.kind: truck diesel engine (pulled unit, not installed in a chassis)

claims.claim: Clean and powerful Trailer Head Engine
claims.evidence: Photos 1 and 2 show this is a standalone pulled engine sitting in an open yard among scrap parts, not part of or attached to a trailer head/chassis.

claims.claim: In excellent condition and ready for work
claims.evidence: No start-up video, compression test, oil check, or running sound is shown; visible surface oxidation and outdoor storage in photos 0-2 do not support 'excellent' condition.
No performance data, dyno reading, or running clip provided in any photo.

risks.risk: Engine may not start or run; internal wear/damage cannot be seen from static photos.
risks.proof: A clear video clip of the engine starting cold and idling, with audible sound.

risks.risk: Corrosion or water ingress from prolonged outdoor tarp storage (seen in photos 1-2) could affect cylinders, electronics, or sensors.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of cylinder bores (via removed injector) and electrical connectors/ECU, plus a dry-storage location photo.

risks.risk: Engine may be incomplete (missing turbo, ECU, wiring harness, oil pan, or other ancillaries) as it's pulled and stored loosely with other parts.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set of the engine alone, including underside and connection points.

risks.risk: The specific DAF engine model/displacement affecting value cannot be confirmed beyond '24 valve' marking.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine ID/serial tag with full alphanumeric code, or the block casting number.
risks.if_unproven: priced at base generic DAF engine tier until model confirmed

proof_requests: Video of the engine starting and idling with sound.
Close-up of the full engine serial/ID plate and block number.
Photos of the engine's underside, oil pan, and all ancillary parts (turbo, ECU, harness) to confirm completeness.
Photo showing current dry storage conditions, not under a tarp outdoors.
response.reason: This is clearly identifiable as a used, pulled DAF diesel engine (24-valve) stored outdoors among scrap parts, not an installed trailer head as claimed; with no proof of running condition or completeness, it must be priced at worst case as a non-verified, possibly non-running core engine.
